scope: Selected C01-C20 requirements measured through distinct real unittest methods and identified retained external evidence. This report does not certify the whole Python suite, remote CI, every legacy external destination, or the full product.

cases.title: Positive module reuse
cases.expected: Two entry objects instantiate one pinned library class; internal parts, parameter overrides, references, and motion state remain independent.

cases.title: Namespaces and composition
cases.expected: Two libraries expose the same lexical class/function names through distinct aliases. Qualification resolves each correctly; alias rename retains the imported nominal identity.

cases.title: Transitive closure
cases.expected: An entry imports A, A imports B; a clean offline resolver uses exactly the supplied pinned bytes and reports the full dependency closure.

cases.title: Positive keyed construction
cases.expected: One generator creates three explicitly keyed asymmetric parts. Expected identities, dimensions, poses, ownership, and own/aggregate mass match a separately authored reference assembly.

cases.title: Key stability
cases.expected: Reorder inputs, insert one key, then remove another. Surviving occurrence/descendant identities and effective inputs remain unchanged; only intended membership changes.

cases.title: Empty and singleton boundaries
cases.expected: Empty and one-entry inputs have declared types, exact counts and mass; valid empty generation produces no phantom object/frame/body. Invalid body types/access still fail when empty.

cases.title: Nested final-input composition
cases.expected: An outer initializer changes a child's keyed input before nested construction. No default-only child survives, no child is duplicated, and final references/values resolve once.

cases.title: Scoped per-key repair
cases.expected: Change one generated public parameter through an occurrence initializer. Siblings and shared library bytes remain unchanged; inspection identifies the override and its origin.

cases.title: UTF-8 and candidate source
cases.expected: A rejected per-key unit edit reports the actual file/hash and candidate byte span, preserves accepted program bytes, and can be repaired against the accepted head.

cases.title: Exact pin failure
cases.expected: Absent file, wrong hash, changed dependency bytes under one name, invalid path, and undeclared dependency each fail explicitly without ambient or network fallback.

cases.title: Module validity failure
cases.expected: Import cycle, conflicting package pin/definition identity, incompatible version/profile, imported scene, or forbidden import-side effect fails before construction. Unrelated packages may reuse a module key without collision.

cases.title: Key/type failure
cases.expected: Duplicate/invalid/missing keys, wrong element type/unit, and an unsupported keyed nesting/type form each return the specified error rather than silently coerce or omit an entry.

cases.title: Access and identity failure
cases.expected: Private traversal, generated shared-span write, same-level duplicate override, and nominal replacement under an unchanged occurrence key fail without partial acceptance.

cases.title: Shape dependency and cycle boundary
cases.expected: Valid lazy pure inputs preserve baseline branch semantics. Prohibited evaluated shape reads, cyclic derivation, and recursive composition—including an empty generated edge—fail distinctly from resource exhaustion.

cases.title: Resource boundaries
cases.expected: The supported maximum and one-over limit are tested for files/bytes, keyed entries, generated objects/depth, dependency work, and serialized output. Failure preserves accepted source and does not claim a partial complete assembly.

cases.title: Mechanical composition
cases.expected: Generated components with prescribed internal following/joints move independently within a moving owner; world transforms and mass match a written reference with no double motion.

cases.title: Release composition
cases.expected: A generated sphere initially carried through an explicit supported grip releases with the existing world-state transfer and gravity trajectory; ownership alone does not keep it attached.

cases.title: Program revision and lifecycle
cases.expected: Change a dependency pin through one atomic candidate; stale expected heads, old cursors/runs/artifacts, retries, cancellation, and independent-process recovery retain the specified program context. Existing `0.1` operations still pass their original cases.

cases.title: Deterministic identity and invalidation
cases.expected: Equivalent source-map ordering follows the adopted canonical hash rule; changing any closure bytes/pins changes the required revision. Old results retain the old identities and are not presented as new output.

cases.title: Actual versioned delivery
cases.expected: Export and retrieve the generated assembly, verify source/program/artifact hashes and authored profile, validate glTF, compare imported geometry and motion, and visually inspect the same artifact. Unsupported output and lost recipe information are reported.
